repo_notes.content: Academic research project on metaheuristics for the 0/1 knapsack problem. Human authorship is the core rule: everything under knapsack-algorithms/src is written by hand without generative AI, while the surrounding ecosystem (knapsack-core, knapsack-bench, build, CI, docs) is developed with AI assistance. When documenting algorithms, describe what the code does as written, citing files and lines; state measured behaviour only when it comes from the bench output; leave assessments of correctness, fixes and improvement ideas out of the wiki, since they belong to the author. Java 25, Maven multi-module build with the Maven Wrapper. Code identifiers are English, project prose and CLI output are Spanish. The canonical documentation and experiment results are published with MkDocs on GitHub Pages at https://dmorfav.github.io/Knapsack/; link there for results instead of restating numbers. Official results live in the results branch, written weekly by the benchmark workflow.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: Introduce the project as a test bench for hand-written metaheuristics on the 0/1 knapsack problem, and state the human-authorship policy for algorithms

page_notes.content: Lead with the problem definition and the split between human-authored algorithms and the AI-assisted ecosystem, as stated in README.md.

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.purpose: Guide users through the Java 25 toolchain, the Maven Wrapper, running tests, the command-line subcommands and building the documentation locally

page_notes.content: Commands run from the repository root. Subcommands are picocli classes in knapsack-bench/src/main/java/org/dmorfav/knapsack/bench/cli. The canonical guide is docs/guia/ejecutar.md.

pages.title: System Architecture
pages.purpose: Explain the four Maven modules, their dependency direction and how a solver is discovered, executed and validated

page_notes.content: Dependency direction: knapsack-algorithms and knapsack-baselines depend only on knapsack-core; knapsack-bench depends on all three. Solvers are discovered with java.util.ServiceLoader.

pages.title: Problem Model
pages.purpose: Document Instance, Item, Solution and Evaluation in knapsack-core

page_notes.content: Also cover the original model.Item and model.Knapsack classes, kept with their public API because the original algorithms import them.

pages.title: Solver Contract
pages.purpose: Document KnapsackSolver, SolverInfo, SolverContext, RunContext and Budget, including seeding, evaluation counting and budget exhaustion

page_notes.content: Explain the family/variant identity that allows several implementations of the same algorithm, and the steps to register a new solver.

pages.title: Instances
pages.purpose: Document the JSON instance format, the Pisinger instance generator and the instances shipped in the instances directory

page_notes.content: Sources of truth: InstanceFiles.java for the format, PisingerGenerator.java and InstanceClass.java for generation. The legacy-* instances come from the original project and use capacity 100. Capacity of generated instances is floor(h * sum(w) / (H + 1)). Declared optima are computed by the optimum and generate commands and verified in CI.

pages.title: Baselines
pages.purpose: Document the reference solvers and bounds used to measure algorithms: greedy by ratio, greedy with best single item, exact dynamic programming and the Dantzig upper bound

page_notes.content: Cover the guarantees each baseline gives (half-optimum for greedy/ratio-best-item, exactness and the n*(C+1) cell limit for dynamic programming, upper bound for Dantzig) and how the GAP is computed against the known optimum or the bound.

pages.title: Algorithms
pages.purpose: Overview of the hand-written metaheuristic implementations and how each is exposed to the bench

page_notes.content: Describe each algorithm as written. The original implementations run unmodified through legacy adapters, use Math.random and therefore ignore the run seed.

pages.title: Harmony Search Family
pages.purpose: Describe the Harmony Search, Improved Harmony Search and Discrete Binary Harmony Search implementations and their parameters

page_notes.content: Cover harmony memory, HMCR, PAR and bandwidth as implemented in knapsack-algorithms.

pages.title: Hill Climbing Family
pages.purpose: Describe the first-ascent and best-ascent hill climbing implementations

page_notes.content: Describe initial solution generation and neighbourhood exploration as implemented in knapsack-algorithms.

pages.title: Bench CLI
pages.purpose: Document the picocli command line with the run, experiment, summarize, report, generate and optimum subcommands, solver validation and the reported metrics

page_notes.content: Cover Main, the cli package, SolverCatalog, SolverRun, Reference and the legacy adapters CountingKnapsack and LegacySolvers, which route every legacy model query through the counted, budgeted context. Solvers run isolated by default: the execution package (SolverExecutor, IsolatedExecutor, WorkerProtocol, SolverWorker and the hidden worker subcommand) starts one JVM per solver, talks JSON Lines over stdin/stdout and enforces a hard limit of the time budget plus 5 s; --in-process runs in the same JVM for debugging.

pages.title: Experiments
pages.purpose: Document the YAML experiment definition, the sequential shuffled execution, the results directory files and the summary metrics

page_notes.content: Cover Experiment, ExperimentPlan, ExperimentRunner, RunRecord, TraceRecord, Manifest, EnvironmentInfo and the stats package. runs.jsonl is the source of truth; summary.csv is derived and can be regenerated with the summarize command. Convergence traces are recorded by RunContext on each feasible improvement. A run that exceeds the hard limit or whose process dies is recorded as failed; after three process failures the solver is disqualified for the rest of the experiment. The manifest records the execution mode.

pages.title: Statistics and Reports
pages.purpose: Document the Friedman, Nemenyi, Wilcoxon and Holm comparison, performance profiles, convergence curves and the generated MkDocs result pages

page_notes.content: Cover Comparison, HypothesisTests, Distributions, Convergence, ChartSpecs and ReportGenerator. Instances are blocks and the measure is the median GAP; failures rank last. Statistical tests are validated against scipy reference values in HypothesisTestsTest. Explain the documented limitations: few instances give low power, timings depend on the machine.

pages.title: Development Workflow
pages.purpose: Document the build configuration, test suites, the GitHub Actions workflows (build, CodeQL, docs, weekly benchmark) and the authorship guardrails

page_notes.content: Include the Maven enforcer rules, JaCoCo coverage, build.yml, qa.yml, docs.yml (MkDocs build and GitHub Pages deploy), benchmark.yml (weekly experiment stored in the results branch) and the Claude Code hooks in .claude/hooks that protect knapsack-algorithms/src and reserve commits for the author. Contributor guarantees: ArchitectureTest (ArchUnit rules on knapsack-algorithms bytecode), SolverContractTest (contract for every registered solver, run isolated), CODEOWNERS, the pull request template with the authorship declaration, and pull-request.yml, which rejects PRs mixing knapsack-algorithms/src with other files or lacking the declaration. The canonical page is docs/guia/contribuir.md.
